## Rule

Two non-zero colors form perpendicular full-line/band structures. The cells at
their intersections currently carry the line color and must be recolored to the
band color; all other cells copy through unchanged.

Equivalent compact form for this generator: the non-zero cells in row 0 and
column 0 are the two perpendicular signature vectors. Their outer product is the
crossing mask. The crossing cell itself contains the line color, so the band
color is the opposite signature color.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
idx = color_index(input[:15, :15])
top = idx[0, :]
left = idx[:, 0]
cross = (top[None, :] > 0) & (left[:, None] > 0)

r = first_nonzero(left)
c = first_nonzero(top)
line_color = idx[r, c]
top_color = max(top)
left_color = max(left)
band_color = left_color if line_color == top_color else top_color

output = input.copy()
output[:, cross] = onehot(band_color)
```

## Cost analysis

Live model (cost 46434 = memory 45939 + params 495): dominated by 10 color-channel intermediates. Each channel: Equal(out_scalar,c) [1,1,15,15] bool 225B; Cast(→float) raw_c [1,1,15,15] float 900B; Mul(raw_c, valid_mask) ch_c [1,1,15,15] float 900B. valid_mask [15,15] float 900B. Plus row_grid/col_grid [15,15] int64 = 225 elems each. Slice with 4 no-op axes.

The gridvec_andfold prototype (cost 37936 = memory 37869 + params 67): grid-vec replaces [15,15] grids with [15,1]/[1,15] (saves 420 params + 420B valid_row/valid_col memory); slice-collapse drops no-op batch/channel axes from Slice (saves 8 params); And-fold replaces Cast(Equal)+Mul(valid_mask) with And(Equal,valid_bool)+Cast (saves raw_c 900B per channel × 10 = 9000B, plus removes valid_mask 900B = 9900B saved, net after adding and_valid bool 225B × 10 = 2250B: saves 7650B).

The v1 rewrite cost is 3,793 (memory 3,598 + params 195). Largest intermediates:
`idx_15x30_f` [1,1,15,30] F32 = 1,800B, `cross_30` [1,1,30,30]
BOOL = 900B, `idx_15x30_u8` [1,1,15,30] UINT8 = 450B, and `idx`
[1,1,15,15] UINT8 = 225B. The final `Where` output is graph output and is
uncounted; passing unchanged cells through `input` avoids rebuilding a 10-channel
one-hot canvas.

The v2 rewrite cost is 1,494 (memory 1,450 + params 44). Largest intermediates:
`cross_b` [1,30,30] BOOL = 900B, `top_fg` and `left_fg` [1,30] F32 = 120B
each, `top_counts`/`left_counts`/`cross_counts` [1,10] F32 = 40B each, and
`target_f` [1,10,1,1] F32 = 40B. Under this overlay formulation the 900B
crossing mask is the practical floor; everything else is vector-sized.

The v4 rewrite cost is 851 (memory 760 + params 91). Largest intermediates:
`Q_basis` [2,30] F32 = 240B, `R_basis` [2,30] F32 = 240B, `C_basis` [4,10]
F32 = 160B, and `top_counts`/`left_counts`/`line_counts` [1,10] F32 = 40B
each. This beats the v2 900B mask floor by moving the whole output assembly into
the final graph-output `Einsum`. Sub-700 would require eliminating at least one
of the charged basis stacks; constants/params polish alone cannot get there.

The v5 exact polish keeps the same 760B memory profile as v4 but lowers params to
79 by reusing the basis vectors for top/left/line color reads. Remaining params:
`axis0` 30, `sel2` 20, `coeff` 16, `bg` 10, `pick1` 2, `batch1` 1. The next exact
step below 839 needs a memory reduction, not parameter shaving.

The v9 exact polish removes only `batch1`: final `Einsum` now multiplies by
`input[:,0,0,0]` selected with the existing `bg` and `axis0` initializers, so the
batch dimension is carried by free input rather than a counted parameter. Cost is
838 (memory 760 + params 78). Remaining params are `axis0` 30, `sel2` 20,
`coeff` 16, `bg` 10, and `pick1` 2. This is probably at the params-only floor
unless a more substantial reconstruction deletes one of `Q_basis`, `R_basis`, or
`C_basis`.

The 2026-06-19 `fold_q_direct_fast` candidate deletes `Q_basis` while preserving
the v9 output formula. Remaining charged tensors are `R_basis [2,30]` = 240B,
`C_basis [4,10]` = 160B, and `top_counts`/`left_counts`/`line_counts [1,10]` =
40B each, for 520B memory; params remain the v9 floor of 78. Static cost and the
full real-input profile are both 598. Expected single-task delta versus the
team-best cost 838 from `K-NeuroGolf-OnnxlyFans/Team_Submission/Backend/manifest.csv`
is `ln(838/598) = +0.3374` points.

The 2026-06-22 `task293_foldbasis_fast` candidate deletes `R_basis` too, so
NEITHER spatial [2,30] stack is materialized. Remaining charged tensors are
`C_basis [4,10]` = 160B and `top_counts`/`left_counts`/`line_counts [1,10]` =
40B each, for 280B memory; params stay at the 78 floor. Static cost AND the full
real-input profile (`--arcgen 266`) are both **358** — verified that the
operand-reordered output Einsum does NOT silently materialize a `[1,10,30,30]`
temp under real inputs. Expected single-task delta vs team-best 838 is
`ln(838/358) = +0.8503` points; vs the 598 prior floor `ln(598/358) = +0.5128`.
**Floor for this formulation = 358.** C_basis cannot be dropped: the output
Einsum needs the four color-role vectors (bg/top/left/line) stacked on a single
`p` axis to contract against `coeff[pqr]` in ONE einsum; splitting into four
addends needs either four full-canvas `[1,10,30,30]` partial outputs + Add (each
charged) or a `[4,10]` stack — which IS C_basis. The three count vectors are the
color roles themselves (irreducible) and Concat requires them as named tensors,
so they coexist with C_basis. No sub-358 lever found without a different additive
output assembly.

  `foldbasis_fast` file (cost 358, points 19.1195). Re-derived the floor: the 3

  `bchw,bdhy,w,y`; line is 3-input) so they cannot be merged into one Einsum, and
  Concat requires them as named [1,10]=40B tensors that coexist with C_basis
  [4,10]=160B → 280B memory floor. Dropping C_basis or the bg-role both require
  the rejected additive assembly (4×full-canvas Add or an equivalent stack). No
  sub-358 lever exists for this formulation. STOPPED at fast-fail; no new
  candidate staged.
- 2026-05-19: gridvec-only (without And-fold) gives only -848 cost. Not worth staging separately.
- The spread advisory suggests crop-to-15×15 could save ~27000B, but not yet explored post-andfold since remaining cost is dominated by the 10-channel Concat/channel intermediates.
- 2026-06-04: Reducing `top + left - idx` over the whole 15×15 crop without
  masking is wrong. Off-grid cells in line columns/rows can carry the line color,
  so `ReduceMax(raw)` picks the line color when line > band. It scored only
  visible 139/267 and truth 1112/2000. Use the tiny crossing-cell
  ArgMax+GatherND role test instead.
- 2026-06-04: Sparse initializer probes (`task293_v6_sparse_inits` and
  `task293_v7_sparse_presafe`) are not official-scoreable. ORT can execute the
  unsanitized sparse model, but the official scorer runs `sanitize_model` and
  then `onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes(strict_mode=True)`, which rejects
  sparse tensors as `Einsum` inputs (`ShapeInferenceError: unsupported type:
  sparse_tensor(float)`). Do not rely on sparse initializers for this task.
- 2026-06-04: Sparse `ScatterND(reduction="add")` repair (`task293_v8_scatter_add`)
  is not a winner. The compact idea is to keep `input` free and add eight scalar
  crossing deltas, but the dynamic index construction alone costs 448B
  (`scatter_idx` 256B + three 64B expanded index lanes), total score is 1,033
  (memory 960 + params 73), and the simple top-color-is-line assumption fails
  visible at 149/267. Making it exact requires more color-role logic and moves
  even farther above the v9 basis model.
- 2026-06-19→2026-06-22 RESOLVED: Folding both `Q_basis` and `R_basis` (358
  static) is now the SHIPPABLE win — see `task293_foldbasis_fast`. The 2026-06-19
  `foldbasis_direct` timeout was NOT inherent to the both-fold; it was an Einsum
  operand-ORDER pathology. Its output equation `pc,bdhy,bexw,qd,re,y,x,pqr->bchw`
  let ORT pick a path that materialized the dense cross-product of the two full
  `[1,10,30,30]` `input` operands (~6.3s/pair → 120s gate timeout). Reordering so
  each `input` copy is ADJACENT to its own small factors — `bdhy,qd,y,bexw,re,x,
  pc,pqr->bchw` — forces ORT to contract each spatial side to a tiny `bqh`/`brw`
  factor FIRST; first-run drops 6308ms→3.8ms, byte-identical output, all gates
  green. Lesson: a both-input-contraction Einsum is NOT intrinsically a timeout;
  fix the operand order before abandoning (#89).
- 2026-06-19: Dropping `C_basis` instead of a spatial basis stack has no clean
  single-output `Einsum` expression yet: bg/top/left/line color-count operands
  must be additively assembled into the role axis, and doing that outside the
  final output would charge full-canvas intermediates or an equivalent stack.
